rounds.text: National Fittings Ltd trades at an attractive valuation with a price-to-earnings ratio of 15.5x [E1] and a price-to-book ratio of 1.58x [E8], both of which sit favorably below their respective sector benchmarks of 36.09x and 3.48x [E6, E7]. The enterprise value to EBITDA ratio of 6.32x also compares exceptionally well against the sector benchmark of 15.77x [E11]. Fundamental performance has demonstrated robust profit momentum, evidenced by a compounded profit growth of 43% over 5 years [E19] and 42% over the trailing twelve months [E21], while the 5-year profit growth of 43% vastly outpaces the 20% share price growth over the same period, signaling that fundamentals are outpacing the stock [E23, E55]. A discounted cash flow model suggests a major margin of safety of 62.0% [E45], and the reverse DCF indicates that the current market price implies an earnings growth of just 4.7% compared to the 18.0% base case assumption [E46]. Furthermore, the company maintains a conservatively financed balance sheet with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.18x [E38] alongside a significant buildup in capital-work-in-progress up 662.5% to Rs 3.05 Cr, pointing toward active growth spending [E40]. Conceded: operating cash flow is negative at Rs -3.87 Cr in Mar 2026 [E35], and promoter holding is low at 34.3% [E59].

The investment case carries severe fundamental and technical risks that undermine its superficial valuation appeal. Most critically, the company experienced a collapse in cash generation as operating cash flow turned negative to Rs -3.87 Cr in Mar 2026, delivering a disastrous cash conversion of -0.42x and free cash flow of -8.96 Cr [E34, E35, E36]. This cash burn is compounded by a sudden surge in borrowings from Rs 5.44 Cr to Rs 15.67 Cr and a ballooning of working capital requirements, with working capital days nearly doubling from 36.1 days to 75.1 days [E39, E62]. Furthermore, earnings quality is suspect because reported profits include Rs 4.78 Cr of other income [E61], while top-line growth over medium-to-long horizons remains lackluster at just 6% over 10 years and 2% over 3 years [E14, E16]. Momentum and institutional backing are entirely absent, with the stock trading below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages, sitting 29.6% off its 52-week high, and carrying low promoter ownership of 34.3% alongside a poor rules-based screen score of 45 out of 100 [E48, E49, E59, E63]. Conceded: the company trades at a favorable P/E of 14.83x against a sector benchmark of 36.09x and has demonstrated strong 5-year profit growth of 42.5% [E6, E58].

Conceded: operating cash flow turned negative to Rs -3.87 Cr and free cash flow dropped to -8.96 Cr in Mar 2026 [E34, E35, E36]. However, this cash burn and the rise in CWIP to Rs 3.05 Cr—a massive 662.5% increase—reflect an active capex build-up and growth spend underway rather than structural failure [E40]. While borrowings increased to Rs 15.67 Cr, the debt-to-equity ratio remains at a conservative 0.18x [E38, E39]. Furthermore, the company maintains a robust 5-year and trailing-twelve-month profit growth of 43% and 42% respectively, vastly outpacing a 10-year share price growth of just 2% and a 1-year return of -11.3%, which highlights how severely fundamentals are leading and decoupling from the depressed stock price [E19, E21, E22, E25, E51, E55]. Finally, trading at a P/E of 14.83x against a sector benchmark of 36.09x and an EV/EBITDA of 6.32x against a sector 15.77x completely compensates for short-term working capital adjustments [E6, E11, E62].

While the bull frames the negative operating cash flow of Rs -3.87 Cr and negative free cash flow of Rs -8.96 Cr as a temporary capex build-up [E35, E36, E40], this cash drain is severely exacerbated by operational inefficiency, as working capital days have more than doubled from 36.1 to 75.1 days [E62]. Conceded: the debt-to-equity ratio remains low at 0.18x [E38]. However, the sharp rise in borrowings to Rs 15.67 Cr from Rs 5.44 Cr [E39] is highly concerning given that operating cash flow was negative and represented -32% of operating profit [E34, E37]. Furthermore, the bull's focus on historical profit growth [E19, E21] ignores the reality that earnings growth is decelerating [E67], highlighted by net profit dropping -88% YoY [E66] and three-year compounded sales growth slowing to a mere 2% [E16]. Finally, the seemingly cheap valuation multiples [E6, E11] are compromised because current earnings are artificially supported by other income of Rs. 4.78 Cr [E61], leading to a rules-based screen score of just 45 out of 100 [E63].
